items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He has recorded with Marian McPartland, Jane Jarvis, the New York Swing Trio, and numerous vocal artists.

ctx.x: Jay Leonhart is a first-call bassist as well as a talented singer and songwriter.

He was born in 1940 in Baltimore, and received his music education at Berklee School of Music and Oscar Peterson’s School for Contemporary Music. By the early ‘60s, Jay was performing with top jazz artists including Mike Longo and Buddy Morrow. He has recorded with Marian McPartland, Jane Jarvis, the New York Swing Trio, and numerous vocal artists. He is currently devoting an increasing amount of time to his songwriting and singing endeavors.
Jay was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 15, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

items.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: She records frequently and can be found in the company of such stellar bassists as Milt Hinton and Jay Leonhart.

ctx.x: In November of 1995, the American Federation of Jazz Societies honored Jane Jarvis with a jazz festival celebrating her 80th birthday and distinguished career in music. Her diverse achievements include record producing for the Muzak Corporation, official organist for the Milwaukee Braves and New York Mets, jazz performing, recording, arranging and an ever-increasing role as a lecturer and spokesperson for jazz education. She is a founding member and pianist for the Statesmen of Jazz, a group of veteran musicians…
Jane was interviewed by Monk Rowe in Los Angeles on September 3, 1995.
